newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks hit by Wall St but end off lows.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks hit by Wall St but end off lows.

text.p: The Australian share market was hit on Wednesday by a tumble on Wall Street, but regained ground in afternoon trade to end off its lows.
The All Ordinaries Index closed down 26.9 points, or 1.01 percent, at 2,623.6 after dipping at one stage below 2,605.
The share price index futures contract closed down 18 points at 2,631, a 7.4 point premium to the physical market.
"The market opened with the futures down about 26 and we retained that bearish tone all day," said Mark Fordree of ANZ Securities in Sydney.
Companies releasing profit results included the Commonwealth Bank and miner WMC Ltd, both in line with market expectations.
The CBA finished nine cents weaker at A$16.28 (US$12.21) after reporting an annual net profit of A$1.078 billion, a slight decline on A$1.119 billion a year earlier.
Its shares fell after the result as the bank warned of a testing year for profits ahead, but recovered in the afternoon along with the rest of the sector.
The ANZ posted the strongest recovery, bouncing 34 cents to end up four cents at A$10.04.
Australia's biggest listed company, BHP, also staged a turnaround, ending up 11 cents at A$17.13 from a low of A$16.78.

Brokers said BHP's rally followed the release of WMC's results -- a 40.9 percent fall to A$228.2 million before abnormals -- and may have reflected relief that the sector offered no unpleasant surprises.
Coca-Cola Amatil continued its fall since the release of flat interim profit results last week, slipping a further 55 cents to A$14.185.
About 5.4 million shares in food group Burns Philp changed hands, including 4.56 million, about 0.9 percent of the issued capital, specialled by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell at A$2.42.
Metal Manufactures, which reported a sharp fall in interim net profit but forecast an improved second half, closed down nine cents at A$3.06.
